thread.title: Are Any Computer Stocks Worth Holding Now, Including Apple? | Seeking Alpha

author: Peter F. Way, CFA
title: Are Any Computer Stocks Worth Holding Now, Including Apple? | Seeking Alpha
text:
Why Read This Report? This is an analysis of how the prices of specific securities are likely to change in the next 3-4 months, based on the way major investment organizations ("institutional investors") have perceived those prospects and made multi-million-dollar trade changes of holdings in their multi-billion-dollar portfolios. It is not a study of years-plus effects of economics, technology, politics, or competitive use of resources on earnings per share of securities. Such studies by others are embedded in their forecasts.
It is a comparison of present-day opportunities for capital gain among many related alternative choices for wealth accumulation as seen by investors with the capital and human resources sufficient to cause such price changes. It is based on how their prior internal organization forecasts, comparable to today's, worked out in the securities markets in time horizons of subsequent shorter-term holding periods.
During the year 2018, daily analysis like this on live selections (before the fact) of over 4,800 top-ranked choices produced net gains (in equities) after losses, at average annual rates of +25%, in a year when the market index of the S&P 500 declined by -7%.
Computer Industry Investments - Now A Tactical Mistake? Figure 1 pictures how the Market-Making [MM] community currently sees the coming price prospects for computer stocks held by its institutional investment clients - as revealed in the way the MMs protect themselves when called upon to put firm capital at risk while providing buyer-seller shares balance to complete multi-million-dollar block trades in these stocks.
Figure 1
(Note: all materials from blockdesk.com have been approved for this article)
For comparison, the MM-expected price range for SPDR S&P500 ETF ( SPY ) appears as the location [15]. That suggests most of these stocks are a less attractive near-term bet on a reward-to-risk basis than the "market" at large.
Beside the quantitative Reward-Risk comparisons, there are qualitative considerations to risk and reward. The odds of their being achieved or incurred and the lengths of time which may be involved are the qualitative dimensions needed in astute portfolio investment selections. Those aspects are examined in Figure 2 for the principal computer and related accessory manufacturers.
My apologies for the sea of data, but this is an industry with nearly a trillion dollars of market capitalization with three-fourths of it in Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) alone. Over a dozen others are present merely as industry-derived activity in accessories. This is an industry in transformation from one of the tools for record-keeping, analysis, and research by professionals, to one which markets to an entertainment, recreation, and enriched communication audience of a public which is less-critically driven. Is this an enviable place for an investor to frequent with risk capital?
Figure 2
Sources: blockdesk.com, Yahoo, Seeking Alpha
Needed perspective comes from columns [S] and [T], showing the market capitalizations of the stocks, and the number of Seeking Alpha readers and contributors indicating a desire to be informed when the stock is referred to in an article or news item.
Market caps are dominated by Apple, with International Business Machines ( IBM ) and HP Inc. ( HPQ ) making up some nine-tenths of the column's near-trillion-dollar total. SA reader requests to stay updated are similarly weighted disproportionally, with additional interest indicated in Western Digital ( WDC ), Stratasys Ltd. ( SSYS ), and Seagate Technology plc ( STX ).
But best near-term prospects are in Mercury Computer ( MRCY ), Universal Display ( OLED ), and Tech Data Corp. (NASDAQ: TECD ), all ahead of AAPL from a near-term portfolio wealth-building objective.
That harsh assessment comes from the analysis of actual market OUTCOMES of MM forecasts made live in the past 5 years, forecasts with upside to downside price expectations balances like those of the present. If coming market price behavior of these stocks resembles what has preceded them, it is mostly an inhospitable place for risk capital to reside.
The details of Figure 2 are as follows: Current-day price range forecasts implied by the hedging actions of MMs putting firm capital at risk to satisfy institutional investor client block trades are seen in [B] and [C]. An upside price change potential of [B] from [D] is in [E], and a measure of the proportions of up to down price change prospects is the Range Index in [G]. Previous examples of similar [G] forecasts are counted in [L], with their net price gain performances indicated in [I]. The proportions of profitable outcomes [H] are a highly significant element of this analysis.
They can be used to weight the achieved upside reward portion of prior similar forecasts and its complement used to weight the price drawdowns actually experienced in the process. Win odds of 75 out of 100 positions are marginal, with 80 and higher desirable. The effect of such weighting of [I] and [F] data in [O] and [P] are netted in [Q]. The rows of Figure 2 are ranked, largest to smallest on [Q].
Significantly, only the top 3 stocks, excluding AAPL, have any significant odds-weighted profitability forecast in the coming 3 months. When the average market-day holding periods [J] of the prior [L] positions are imposed on [Q], the RATES of return to be expected (in basis points per day) further separate the potential outcomes. Only these top 3 have any significant payoff promise for investors attempting to build equity investment portfolio wealth.
Additional perspective on this kind of evaluation comes from the comparison of AAPL expectations with those of market-index ETF prospects, such as in SPDR S&P500 Index ETF ( SPY ) and with the best-ranked issues in a population of over 2,600 widely-held and actively-held stocks and ETFs. They are shown in the blue rows at the bottom of Figure 2.
The Win Odds of SPY at 69 are similar to those of AAPL (69), while the Reward and Risk elements are also smaller. AAPL has more volatility than the present market - no kidding! But only the downside of volatility is Risk to the wealth-builder; the upside is opportunity.
SPY's [F]-column data of -4.2% is actually larger than its achieved +1.5% rewards [I] from prior similar forecasts. With a 69/31 odds split in favor of the +1.5%, the net [Q] for SPY turns into a negative -0.4%. AAPL's trade-offs between 69% of its +2.6% achieved gains and 31% of its exposed -7.7% risk also comes out a negative -0.8% net in [Q].
Taking the AAPL analysis a step further, its time investment in prior positions [J] of 51 days yields a prospective rate of loss on its [Q] of -1.6 basis points per day in [R], the equivalent of a -5.6% CAGR. MRCY's 19.2 bp/day is the equivalent of a CAGR of 101%; 5 bp/day is a +20% CAGR.
While MRCY and OLED and TECD's bp/day are superior performance compared to anything else in the Computer Industry investment alternatives, they are not in the top tier of the large population of parallel present forecasts. The best of that population averages Win Odds of 87, or 7 profitable positions of every 8. Applied to prior forecasts net profits of +10.1% in 39 days of holding time, their average bp/day of +22.2 equals a CAGR of 97%.
MRCY, OLED, And AAPL, Recent Price Range Expectations Pictured Figure 3
The vertical lines here are ranges of likely coming prices expected near term, at the date of the forecast. The dates are once-a-week (Thursdays) extractions of forecasts determined every market day. They cover the most recent two-year period.
The red flag on MRCY's Sample Size in the data row of Figure 3 is simply an alert that in the past 5 years of 1,261 daily forecasts of the most likely highs and lows of its coming prices in the next 3-4 months, only 19 days had Range Indexes as extreme as this day's. A 4 Range Index means that less than ½ of 1% of the expected price range was in prices below this day's $48.34 market price. The other 96% of the forecast range was above today's $48.34, all the way up to $57.16.
We look to prior forecasts which have the same upside to downside proportions as are seen today for indications of what prices are likely to be coming near-term. A sample small enough to be influenced by only a few extreme forecasts could be misleading. That likely won't be a problem with 19 forecasts to be averaged, but perhaps with only, say a dozen, it could.
The small blue picture at the bottom of Figure 3 shows the frequency of forecast Range Indexes for MRCY, and how they are less frequent down at this RI level. The odds for reaching profitable prices should, under normal circumstances, be related to forecast proportions. In the case of MRCY here, its Win Odds of 84 out of 100 are reassuring to a wealth-building objective. Those odds are the average experience of these 19 prior forecast experiences.
Comparing Win Odds among potential investment alternative competitor securities is a common task set by careful skilled investors. Other dimensions subject to examination this way are the size of the sample's average net % price gain payoffs (+11.4% for MRCY) and the extent of price drawdowns (-4.6%) in pursuit of the payoff potentials.
These considerations all are qualitative factors in selecting equity investments, and individual investors may favor each of them in different degrees. "Sauce for one goose" may not be preferable for another "gander". That is what provides liquidity in securities markets. But when markets favor one qualitative factor unduly over another, price extremes occur.
Figures 4 and 5 provide recent price range forecast histories for OLED and AAPL along with their qualitative considerations for your appraisal.
Figure 4
Figure 5
It appears that MRCY offers a far more assuring combination of Win Odds, % Payoffs, and rates of near-term price gain prospects with smaller prior price drawdowns than AAPL. OLED holds out the potential for much more sizable payoffs than AAPL with the same to slightly better odds of a profitable outcome.
But it recognizes the likelihood of interim double-digit price drawdowns on the way to realizing those gains. If that kind of emotional cost (a temporary discomfort, since the achieved gains within the two-month average holding period of 43 market days turn out to be substantial from 221 position closeouts) is not a good fit for you, then a second computer holding choice may be better deferred. The TECD and RAVN price range forecasts lack sufficiently strong samples of prior experience to encourage a capital commitment now.
Other choices, including AAPL, have present forecasts with histories on an odds-weighted basis which are not encouraging to a wealth-building mission near-term.
Comparisons Outside Of The Computer S tocks Realm The lower lines of the Figure 2 table provide a wider perspective, in the MM forecasts for the SPDR S&P 500 Index ETF ( SPY ) as a generalized "market investment" and an average of over 2,600 other stocks and ETFs, in the same MM price range forecast presentation format of the computer industry stocks.
The SPY modestly negative outlook is reinforced by the forecast population average. As usual, there are the exceptions available from careful selection of securities experiencing out-of-average circumstances. Averages of the top ten such are noted under the population data.
The MMs are drawn into these issues by their substantial world-wide information-gathering people resources and the extensive business connections of their institutional investment organization clients. Often the attractive price-change opportunities which exist are in securities less frequently traded in the volumes dictated by the multi-billion-dollar scale of the MM client portfolios. Negotiated block trades usually are required, typically with the temporary support of MM capital. Thus, our analysis becomes aware of them.
Universal Display Corporation is an example. It has been part of our forecast population for over 6 years, starting at prices one third of the present. Its ticker symbol is an acronym for "Organic Light-Emitting Display" crystals, now an integral part of most computer and smartphone screen production.
At times when market-average prospects are not encouraging to ordinary portfolio tactics and strategies, it may be particularly advantageous to explore the out of the ordinary.
Conclusion Mercury Computer ( MRCY ) appears at this point in time to be the most attractive of very few computer stocks for investors interested in portfolio wealth-building by capital gains. With concerns over the general equity market's current pricing, many other computer stocks are likely to reflect the general adjustments which occur. AAPL, with its market capitalization, is almost certain to participate, in both directions. Guilt by association.
But just because longer-term recovery by weight of inertial position may be assured, the time investment in securities which make full recovery back to where they are now - that time is a complete loss. It could be productive, compounding earlier gains, instead of simply marching in place. A broader view of alternative prospects offers competitive advantages others consumed by conventional confusion tend to ignore.
Disclaimer: Peter Way and generations of the Way Family are long-term providers of perspective information, earlier helping professional investors and now individual investors, discriminate between wealth-building opportunities in individual stocks and ETFs. We do not manage money for others outside of the family but do provide pro bono consulting for a limited number of not-for-profit organizations.
We firmly believe investors need to maintain skin in their game by actively initiating commitment choices of capital and time investments in their personal portfolios. So, our information presents for D-I-Y investor guidance what the arguably best-informed professional investors are thinking. Their insights, revealed through their own self-protective hedging actions, tell what they believe is most likely to happen to the prices of specific issues in coming weeks and months. Evidences of how such prior forecasts have worked out are routinely provided in the SA blog of my name. First half of January has produced over a hundred profitable position closeouts.
